sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 opens the Medford atlas: its upper part carries the key map of the town at 600 feet to an inch, an inset of New Jersey locating Medford, the index of streets and specials, the legend and notes on the water works and fire department, and is not part of the georeferenced map. The map, below a heavy line, shows at 50 feet to an inch the north-eastern corner of the business district east of Broad, between the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad at the top left and Branch at the bottom, with north towards the top of the page. Most of it is taken up by the yard of Joseph H. Haines and Sons, threshers, farm implement dealers and builders' finish, lumber, fertilizer, coal and wood merchants: a lumber ware house, sash, door and blinds ware house, hay and straw baling house, thresher shop, saw mill, roof covering and lime ware house and many open lumber piles, crossed by a curving siding. Beside it are the Medford Concrete Co., makers of concrete blocks and pipe, with drying ovens and piles of cement pipe and blocks, two cranberry ware houses on Broad and the Standard Oil Co. pumping station and tanks at the top. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Medford Branch runs down the right side of the yard, with cordwood piled along it and vacant land beyond. Along the bottom, Sibylline Alley, marked as an arbitrary name, and two private drives serve a row of frame dwellings facing Branch.
notes: Only the map below the heavy line is georeferenced; the key map (600 ft to an inch), index and legend above it are left out of the mask.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Broad and Branch, now Broad Street and Branch Street) and a derived point 300 ft north along Broad at the atlas scale; low confidence.
Both railroads (West Jersey and Seashore, and the P.R.R. Medford Branch) are gone; the modern reference has no running line here.
Tidswell Avenue, a modern street from Broad Street to Branch Street, is not drawn.

Key map (600 ft), index, legend and water/fire notes in the upper part (left out); below a heavy line the map at 50 ft: Broad to the P.R.R. Medford Branch, W.J.&S. R.R. to Branch; J. H. Haines & Sons yard, Medford Concrete Co., Standard Oil Co. One part.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the business centre of Medford at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned on the page so that north points to the left: Main Street runs across the sheet from left to right, lettered N. Main on the left and S. Main on the right of the Bank and Union crossing. Above Main Street the sheet shows the blocks between Branch, Church, Bank and Coates, cut by Charles St. and bounded at the top by Filbert; below Main Street it shows the blocks between Cedar, Union and Friends Av, with Maple St. and Cherry at the bottom. Main Street is lined with stores and dwellings: a bank and drug store at the Bank corner, the post office, a harness shop, tenements, the Indian Chief Hotel, a bakery, printing office, paint and oil store and the fire department's engine house and bell. The public school stands on Church between Filbert and Charles, the Baptist Church on Bank near Filbert, and the I.O.O.F. Hall on Charles St.; a public garage for 20 cars is on Maple St. Away from Main Street the blocks hold frame dwellings with stables, sheds and wagon and auto sheds, and a large horse shed lies between Union and Friends Av. Charles St. is drawn only 20 feet wide and Maple St. 15 feet. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are drawn along the main streets, and the sheet's neighbours are marked in the margins: sheet 1 and 7 to the left, 5 above, 3 to the right and 6 below.
notes: The sheet is turned: north points to the left of the page.
Modern names add the suffix Street to Branch, Church, Bank, Coates, Filbert, Cedar, Union and Cherry; N. and S. Main are North and South Main Street.
Charles St. (20 ft) and Maple St. (15 ft) are drawn too narrow for the edge detector; their five junctions were hand-picked on the drawn centrelines.
Post Office Lane, a modern lane off North Main Street, is not drawn.
Business centre at 50 ft, turned (north to the left): N./S. Main, Bank, Union, Branch, Church, Charles St., Filbert, Coates, Cedar, Maple St., Friends Av, Cherry. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers South Main Street in Medford from Friends Av. and Coates at the top of the sheet south to the concrete bridge over the South Branch of Rancocas Creek at the bottom, at 50 feet to an inch with north to the top. Maple St. meets Friends Av. at the top left; Poplar and South run east from South Main Street. The northern blocks are the southern edge of the business centre: a motion picture house, a livery, stores and the Medford House hotel with its stable and long rows of horse sheds behind it on Coates. Further south South Main Street is lined with frame dwellings, an undertaker, a painting shop and two garages, a private garage of concrete block and a public garage for six cars. East of South Main Street lie Friend's Cemetery and Odd Fellow's Cemetery, with the Hicksite Friends Meeting House and the Friends School, the latter used only once a year, on South; hot beds and a cranberry ware house stand on the vacant land at the right edge. The southern third of the sheet is almost empty land sloping to the creek, which crosses the sheet from left to right and is spanned by the concrete bridge carrying South Main Street and a 6-inch water main. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn on South Main Street, Poplar and South. The sheet adjoins sheet 2 above and sheet 4 below.
notes: South is now South Street; Coates is Coates Street; Poplar has no modern counterpart in the reference data.
Placed from three points (two detected, one hand-picked on Maple St., which is drawn about 10 ft wide); the lower half of the sheet has no control of its own.
Allen Avenue, a modern street off South Main Street, is not drawn.
S. Main from Friends Av/Coates south to the S. Branch of Rancocas Creek; Maple St., Poplar, South; Friends' and Odd Fellows' cemeteries. 50 ft, one part.

sheet-4-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 4 is the main map of the sheet, covering South Medford south of the South Branch of Rancocas Creek at 50 feet to an inch, with north about 27 degrees to the left of the top of the page. Mill and S. Main leave the concrete bridge at the top of the sheet together and diverge southward, Mill running straight down the left side and S. Main diagonally to the lower right; Chapel Av. branches east from S. Main at the top and Trimble crosses between the two roads at the bottom. The wedge between Mill and S. Main is filled by the Star Glass Co.'s Factory No. 1, marked not in operation, with its furnaces, lehr, gas producers, ware houses, a long storage shed and a lumber shed. Elsewhere the part shows frame dwellings along Mill, S. Main, Chapel Av. and Trimble, the South Medford Mission and a cement-floored garage on Chapel Av., and a strip of the creek's south branch along the left. The open land west of Mill reaches down to the creek, which winds across the upper left corner. Two insets are drawn on the same sheet behind heavy lines: Chapel Av. further east at the upper right and the Medford Water Works one mile south of the post office at the lower left; both are separate parts. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are drawn along the roads.
notes: Mill, S. Main and Trimble are now Mill Street, South Main Street and Trimble Street; S. Main continues south as Stokes Road.

Placed from two detected junctions on Trimble (with Mill and with S. Main) as a helmert; the modern Chapel Avenue, Mill Street and South Main Street junction lies where the sheet draws the bridge end and was not used. Low confidence.
The Star Glass Co. works are marked 'not in operation'.

South Medford at 50 ft: part 1 (main) Mill, S. Main, Chapel Av, Trimble, Star Glass Co.; part 2 (upper-right inset, own arrow) Chapel Av further east; part 3 (lower-left inset, own arrow) Medford Water Works 1 mile S of P.O. on Mill.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Chapel Avenue further east (dog kennels, lots 1101-1103) (no street junction drawn; needs hand-picked control from a modern feature on Chapel Avenue east of the main part).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Medford Water Works Co., 1 mile south of the post office, on Mill and the South Branch of Rancocas Creek (no street junction drawn; needs hand-picked control (the Mill Street creek crossing or the works site) at about 1 mile south of the post office).

sheet-5-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 5 is the main map of the sheet, covering the residential blocks east of the centre of Medford at 50 feet to an inch with north to the top. Filbert runs down the left side and North down the right; Branch, Church, Mulberry and Bank cross the part from left to right, Walnut St. runs between Branch and Mulberry, and Coates is lettered at the lower left. The blocks are divided into house lots built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings with stables, sheds and auto houses. The M. E. Church and its church yard occupy the corner of Branch and Filbert, and the Baptist Cemetery fills most of the block south of Mulberry between Walnut St. and North. Further south the part shows a garage with a cement floor on Filbert, a paint shop and a cranberry ware house on Bank, and a large vacant block, numbered 15, between Bank and the bottom of the sheet. Several streets carry their drawn widths: Walnut St. 17 feet, Church 25 feet, Mulberry 35 feet. A heavy line in the lower right corner encloses part 2, a separate strip of Branch and Church St. further east. Water pipes of 4 inches and hydrants are drawn along most streets.
notes: Walnut St. is now McClain Avenue; Branch, Church, Mulberry, Bank, Filbert, North and Coates take the suffix Street today.
Walnut St. (17 ft) and the Church Street junction with North were hand-picked; the detector cannot pair streets drawn narrower than 22 ft.
Bookkeepers Lane, a modern lane, appears to follow a 12 to 14 ft alley drawn between Filbert and Walnut St.; it was not used.

East of the centre at 50 ft: part 1 (main) Filbert, North, Branch, Church, Mulberry, Bank, Walnut St. (now McClain Av), Coates; part 2 (lower-right inset, own arrow) Branch and Church St. further east.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Branch and Church St. further east (lots 96-205) (no street junction drawn (two parallel streets only); needs hand-picked control on Branch Street and Church Street east of North Street).

sheet-6-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 6 is the main map of the sheet, covering the west side of Medford along Union at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned on the page so that north points to the left. Cherry runs across the top of the part from Cedar, lettered in the top left corner, to Union, which runs down the right half of the sheet. North of Cherry a row of frame dwellings and a cranberry ware house face the street. Along Union stand the Friends Meeting House with its Sunday school and horse sheds, St. Peter's Episcopal Church with its horse shed, and scattered frame dwellings with stables, a silo and storage sheds; the large lot between Cherry and the heavy line is mostly open, with a private barn. Water pipes of 4 inches and hydrants are drawn on Cherry and Union. A heavy line in the lower left encloses part 2, a separately drawn strip of Union further out of town, and the area west of that line is marked vacant beyond.
notes: The sheet is turned: north points to the left of the page, about 81 degrees anticlockwise.
Placed from two detected junctions along Cherry (with Union and with Cedar) as a helmert; low confidence for the lower part of Union.
Cherry, Union and Cedar are now Cherry Street, Union Street and Cedar Street. Allen Avenue, a modern street crossing Union Street, is not drawn.
West side at 50 ft, turned (north to the left): part 1 (main) Cherry, Union, Cedar corner, Friends Meeting Ho., St. Peter's; part 2 (lower-left inset, own arrow) Union further west.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Union further west (lots 501-503, blocks 6 and 7) (no street junction drawn; needs hand-picked control on Union Street west of the main part).

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 7 is the main map of the sheet, covering the north end of Medford's business district at 50 feet to an inch with north to the top. N. Main runs down the left half of the sheet, Charles St. down the middle and Broad along the right; Cedar crosses the lower left corner and Branch the bottom. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad crosses the sheet from left to right above the middle, with its passenger station and express office, platforms, a freight house and stock crib, and a siding curving down to the Kirby Bros. feed mill and coal shed. Below the railroad are the Medford Textile Mills, makers of hosiery, a knitting mill, a large public garage and a smaller garage, an auto repair shop and a cranberry house with a gasoline engine, among frame dwellings on N. Main and Broad; a driveway runs from Charles St. to Broad. North of the railroad the Medford Gas Co. works with an iron gasometer stand beside a vacant field, and dwellings line N. Main. A heavy line at the upper right encloses part 2, a separately drawn strip of N. Main further north. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along N. Main and Branch.
notes: N. Main is now North Main Street; Charles, Broad, Cedar and Branch take the suffix Street today.

Placed as a helmert from two points on Branch (with N. Main, detected, and with Broad, as measured by the detector in an earlier run); the upper half of the sheet has no control of its own. Low confidence.
The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad is gone; Railroad Avenue appears to follow its line but was not used. Charles St. is drawn about 15 ft wide at Branch.

North end at 50 ft: part 1 (main) N. Main, Charles St., Broad, Cedar, Branch, W.J.&S. R.R. with station, Kirby Bros. feed mill, Medford Textile Mills, Medford Gas Co.; part 2 (upper-right inset, own arrow) N. Main further north.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: North Main further north (blocks 26 and 27, lots 801-803) (no street junction drawn; needs hand-picked control on North Main Street north of the railroad).
